title: Staged deprecation and client migration waves for structured outputs and streaming tools
creator: Alex Morgan
description: Purpose: define a low-friction, observable, and reversible deprecation path for behavioral changes to the Core API surface (streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured output schemas). Scope covers hosted API v1 -> v2 behavioral deltas, SDK flag usage patterns, server-side compatibility shims, and the regression harness that will gate rollout. Deliverables: migration wave spec (client cohorts + opt-in flags), regression test matrix, SDK migration guide drafts, monitoring dashboards and SLO/rollback criteria, and a communication plan for developer-facing notices and changelog entries.
acceptance_criteria: A documented migration wave plan with 3 client cohorts (pilot, staged, global) and enrollment criteria
Behavioral feature flags implemented server-side with clear opt-in and opt-out semantics documented
SDKs (JS/Python) expose a single migration path and deprecation warning surface across streaming and tool-calls
Backwards-compatibility regression suite runs in CI and covers: streaming boundary conditions, tool-call schema variants, and structured-output parser regressions
Runbook with metrics (error rate, malformed-structured-output, latency p50/p95, client opt-in ratio) and rollback thresholds is approved by SRE and Product
Customer-facing migration guide published in docs and linked from console notices
migration_plan: Phase 0 - Internal pilot: release v2 behind behavior flags in canary runtime. Target: infra and Redwood internal teams. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 1 - External pilot: invite 10 key customers (opt-in) with SDK feature flag. Collect compatibility logs and parser failures. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 2 - Staged rollouts: enable default for 20% of non-enterprise traffic with automatic fallback to v1 variant on parser regressions. Duration: 6 weeks.

Phase 3 - Global switch: flip default to v2 across hosted API after metrics and tests green. Provide 60-day grace period where v1 endpoints remain available for a set of enterprise customers by request.
Opt-out path: customers can set header X-Redwood-Compat: v1 or attach SDK flag to maintain prior behavior for the grace period
Edge cases: streaming + function-calls combined behavior will prefer backward-compatible framing unless client explicitly opts into new framing via 'framing_mode' flag

notes: Key trade-offs discussed: stricter structured-output schemas improve downstream reliability but increase short-term client parsing failures. To reduce noise, we'll initially accept both legacy and strict schema variants and emit deprecation warnings. We will include example migration snippets for streaming + function-calls where framing changes. Ensure SDKs convert legacy framing automatically when safe.
